faq.q: Can I watch the F1 race from a boat in Marbella?
faq.a: Not directly — the circuit is landlocked. But you can anchor near the coast and stream the race on board, or head to Puerto Banús after qualifying for the atmosphere. Many guests charter a boat for the weekend and watch the race from a beach club or villa, then celebrate on the water.

faq.q: What is the best boat for an F1 weekend group of 10?
faq.a: The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers plenty of deck space and a flybridge for sunbathing — great for groups. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) is a more affordable option at €749/2h. For a premium experience, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) includes a free jet ski.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book for F1 2043?
faq.a: At least 3 months, ideally 6. Marbella is a global destination, and F1 weekends see high demand. Boats like the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) and K80 (24m, 12 pax) are often booked months ahead. Early booking also locks in better rates.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), the 2-hour rate is €749 all-in.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks on board?
faq.a: Yes, you can bring your own food and additional drinks. The provided snacks and beverages are complimentary. Many guests bring a cooler with premium champagne or a catered platter. Just avoid glass bottles on the boat for safety.

faq.q: Where does the boat depart from?
faq.a: All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella's iconic marina. It is a 5-minute drive from the F1 circuit and 10 minutes from Marbella's Golden Mile. The marina has parking, restaurants, and shops — perfect for pre-boarding meet-ups.

faq.q: What is the cancellation policy for F1 weekend?
faq.a: Standard policy: free cancellation up to 14 days before departure. For F1 weekends, a 50% deposit is required at booking, refundable if cancelled 30+ days out. We recommend travel insurance for last-minute changes. Contact us via WhatsApp for specific dates.

faq.q: Are there any age restrictions for children?
faq.a: Children are welcome on all boats. Life jackets for all sizes are provided. The skipper will brief safety rules. For boats with jet skis (Mangusta 80 variants), minimum age for riding is 16 with a valid licence. No upper age limit.

data.body_html:
The Marbella F1 Grand Prix 2043 is set to be one of the most glamorous weekends on the Costa del Sol. With the race circuit just minutes from Puerto Banús, a yacht charter offers the ultimate way to combine high-octane racing with Mediterranean luxury. Whether you are celebrating a win or just soaking up the atmosphere, this itinerary shows you how to make the most of the weekend from the water.

Why a Yacht Charter for the F1 Weekend?

Marbella transforms during the F1 Grand Prix. Hotels and beach clubs fill up, but a private boat gives you space, flexibility, and a front-row seat to the marina buzz. From Boat Rental Marbella, you can choose from 17 vessels ranging from 5 to 12 guests. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) at €4,719 for 4 hours includes a free jet ski — ideal for adrenaline seekers. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) at €749/2h is a more budget-friendly option without compromising on style.

Friday: Arrival and Sunset Cruise

Arrive in Marbella and check into your hotel or villa. By late afternoon, head to Puerto Banús for a sunset cruise. The Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax, €749/2h) is perfect for an introductory sail. Cruise past the Golden Mile, anchor near Cala del Faro, and watch the sun dip behind La Concha mountain. Drinks and snacks are included — just bring your F1 cap. Return to port by 9 PM for dinner at one of the marina's seafood restaurants.

Saturday: Qualifying Day and Beach Hopping

Qualifying starts around 2 PM, but your morning is free. Charter the Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax) for a 4-hour trip. Depart at 10 AM, cruise east to Cabo Pino for a swim stop, then head back to Puerto Banús by 1 PM. Watch qualifying from the boat's cabin (streamed via onboard Wi-Fi) or from a beach club with a view. After qualifying, take the boat to Estepona for a late lunch — the old town is a 10-minute walk from the marina.

Sunday: Race Day — The Main Event

Race day is the highlight. Book the Mangusta 80 (Grey) (24m, 12 pax, €4,719/4h) for the full experience. Depart at 11 AM, cruise to a quiet anchorage off San Pedro de Alcántara. The skipper will set up a shaded deck with snacks and drinks. Stream the race live on the boat's TV system or listen on the radio. After the podium, cruise back to Puerto Banús where the celebrations spill onto the docks. The jet ski included with the Mangusta 80 adds an extra thrill — ride it around the bay as the sun sets.

Monday: Recovery and Departure

Before you leave, take a gentle morning cruise on the Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax). This catamaran is stable and spacious — ideal for a relaxed farewell. Head to Cala Cortés for a final swim, then return to port by 1 PM. If you have time, explore the Río Verde area or grab a late breakfast at a chiringuito. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, and insurance — no stress, just unwind.

Tips for a Smooth F1 Weekend Charter

  • Book early: F1 2043 will see high demand. Reserve your boat 3-6 months ahead.
  • Check the weather: October in Marbella averages 22°C sea temperature and 24°C air — light jackets for evenings.
  • Plan parking: Puerto Banús has paid parking garages; arrive early to secure a spot.
  • Bring sunscreen: The Mediterranean sun is strong even in October.
  • Use WhatsApp for enquiries: We respond fastest there for custom quotes and last-minute bookings.
